title: CPU riders escape repeated ramp wrecks sooner (#641)
summary: Escalated CPU recovery now assists after a rider's second return to a checkpoint and relocates it after the third, 320-500 ft ahead, instead of the fourth return and 80 ft.
details: The old placement could drop a rider back into the failed corner or jump approach. Finish and Enduro gate bounds, the maximum skip, clearance checks and stall/clearing rules are unchanged. This is the owner-authorized authored recovery layer, not original driving. Full default-length host races, four CPUs, idle player (wrecks before to after; last CPU finish before to after): sx15 155 to 126, 591.50 s to 488.39 s; sx03 50 to 48, 405.65 s to 425.52 s (19.88 s slower despite fewer wrecks); sx05 58 to 49, 438.67 s to 398.06 s; env05endl 13 to 13, unchanged; nat01, sx12 and env06st had no wrecks and match exactly. The headless example gained per-seat wreck telemetry, working --help and --require-finish, and an SX15 /play.html regression joined the content group.
limitation: One seed per course, host runs only; not an all-seed sweep. Substantial natural wrecks remain, and original-physics parity is not established. The Expert seed-7 sweep already finished through an existing fallback, so this reduces repeated failures and delay rather than fixing a hard stall.
